narrative:
The model estimates a 17% chance that you will fail your final year. That is a low but non-zero risk: most students with a similar profile pass, but the school treats even that level of risk as enough to require remedial courses. It is a precautionary flag, not a certainty.

The strongest signals in your profile actually pushed toward passing. Your past class failures were the most influential factor; you have none, matching the average among students who passed, so this reduced your predicted risk. Your father’s education was next: he completed higher education, a level more common among passers than most other education categories, so it also worked in your favor. Third, your intention to pursue higher education was influential; you said yes, as did every passer in the comparison group, so this too pushed toward passing. The failure flag therefore comes from weaker signals elsewhere, not from your top three drivers.

To improve, protect the strengths the model recognizes: keep your record free of failures, maintain strong attendance, and keep your intention to continue studying. Also use family support and structure your very high free time, which is less typical among passers, into regular study.
